description: We are team Starchitects! fellow alumni of the SHE ORBITS Space Exploration Summer School 2026, excited to collaborate together, and follow our passion of exploring our cosmos!!!
summary:
Eight NASA machines—the Apollo laser mirrors, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner, Opportunity, InSight, Ingenuity, Voyager 1, and Pioneer 10—that were abandoned on the Moon, Mars, and deep space are the subject of the interactive, narrative website Ghost Rovers. By responding to four questions, each machine narrates its own tale in the first person: Why was I sent? How did I operate? What did I discover? Now, where am I? Visitors can shoot a laser at the Moon, block Opportunity's sunlight with dust, compare the air on Earth and Mars, and observe how long radio communications take to reach far-off spacecraft as they scroll across the page, which takes them from the Moon to Mars to deep space.
Using information verified against NASA mission sites and NASA photos, the project addresses the challenge by simplifying the complex mission history into an understandable narrative for those 14 years of age and older as well as new space enthusiasts. It is significant because these devices enabled the missions of today, and their tales demonstrate that a silent space craft is not forgotten.
details:
What it does and how it works: Ghost Rovers is a free, interactive website that tells the stories of eight NASA machines left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space: the Apollo laser mirrors, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner, Opportunity, InSight, Ingenuity, Voyager 1 and Pioneer 10. Each machine speaks in the first person and answers four questions: Why was I sent? How did I work? What did I find out? Where am I now? As visitors scroll, the page colors shift from the Moon to Mars to deep space. Four small interactives show how the hardware worked: firing a laser at the Moon and waiting for the echo, blocking Opportunity’s sunlight with dust, comparing Earth and Mars air for Ingenuity, and sliding through radio delays out to Voyager 1.

 

Benefits. :It works in any browser on a phone or laptop, with no download or login. It turns dense mission history into short, plain-language stories for ages 14 and up and for people hearing about these missions for the first time, and it links to the NASA pages behind the facts.

 

Intended impact: We want visitors to feel a personal connection to these machines and to see that a silent spacecraft is not a forgotten one. Their work led to later missions, such as Perseverance passing Opportunity’s driving record and NASA’s planned SkyFall helicopters building on Ingenuity.

 

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript (no frameworks), hosted free on GitHub Pages. No special hardware. Facts come from NASA mission pages, and the pictures are NASA images.

 

Creativity: We used a consistent four-question card for every machine, and interactives that let visitors discover the engineering instead of reading a list.

 

Factors we considered: Accuracy (facts checked against NASA mission pages), accessibility
